title: Co-Sprout: Regionalism Pavillion
gallery_text:
"In today’s cities, with constant demolition and rebuilding, there’s almost no hope left for architectural and cultural continuity. Old houses are living history; if history disappears, what foundation do we have? The only “seeds” that remain are in the countryside, and I hope they can still sprout. "

                			          — Wang Shu

answers.interest: I am interested in this course because I imagine it would help me bridge digital-twin data, generative AI, and urban decision-making. Where I want to use simulation and agent-based modeling to test how design scenarios perform over time. The course’s understanding of simulation as a way of making arguments also aligns with my critical interest in exposing the assumptions, exclusions, and values embedded in computational models.
answers.suggestions: I would be interested if we can maybe touch on digital-twin data pipeline showing how GIS and BIM information, such as GeoJSON, CityJSON, or IFC data, can be cleaned, translated, and connected to a simulation.
